learner_operation: Solve a small consistent dependent linear system using Gauss-Jordan elimination, identify pivot/free variables, and select its full one-parameter vector solution.

fixed_features.feature: Small real linear system, one free variable, complete vector solution and five-choice radio response
fixed_features.justification: The KP practice, canonical example and tutorial support this contract; observed easy workloads use only a few elementary row operations.

fixed_features.feature: Normal default always has nonzero slopes/constants in both basic coordinates; pivots x/y and free z; two row additions
fixed_features.justification: Observed implementation constraint, not an accepted instructional necessity. Source constant-coordinate/zero-constant/rank-one cases and canonical free-y case contradict fixing these roles.

answer_roles.eligible_variation: Read from pivot columns; canonical example makes y free with z constant. Same-method assignments must not be inferred fixed from most source examples.
answer_roles.observed: Default fixes x/y basic and z free. Optional source profiles add rank-one y-free two-coordinate vectors, but no ordinary calls select them and no canonical three-coordinate y-free profile exists.

answer_roles.eligible_variation: Zero/nonzero slopes and constants, including source cancellation yielding x=0 or x=4.
answer_roles.observed: Default excludes every zero slope and samples only nonzero constants; valid zero-slope and equal-coordinate explicit cases fail because of bank construction.

answer_roles.role: Correct vector and distractor component arrangement
answer_roles.eligible_variation: Correctness must follow the system, independent of modal answer components or position.
answer_roles.observed: The fixed four error recipes replicate the correct first component twice and second component three times in most ordinary banks, exposing their intersection as the key.

coverage.result: All 11 declared profiles reproduce original system coefficients and all five mathematical choices at identity parameters. Three current easy source profiles are rejected as unknown; canonical free-y family is unavailable.

coverage.case: Normal easy construction before and after rejection
coverage.result: 60 seeds 90101..90160 yielded 60 proposals/60 survivors; no resampling in this small sample. Construction fixes all normal decision roles described above. Explicit valid zero-slope and equal-coordinate boundary cases reject.

coverage.case: Exact batch versus independent sample after delivery
coverage.result: 5/5 batch and 60/60 fresh records survive captured-inventory deduplication and easy filtering. Modal shortcut remains 5/5 batch, 59/59 conditional fresh (59/60 including abstention).

counterfactuals.change: Hold seed 90217, constants [1,4], second free coefficient -3 and mix [1,1] fixed; change first RREF free coefficient 2 to -2.
counterfactuals.expected: First solution coordinate changes from 1-2z to 1+2z; previous vector must become a rejected choice. Prompt, RREF and explanation must change consistently.
counterfactuals.observed: Both records display the expected changed equations and solution. Native grader accepts each new key and rejects the old base vector in the changed system. Screenshots 017/018 visually verified.
counterfactuals.justification: The tutorial and practice require solving the actual coefficient relationships. This relevant change alters the solution set.

counterfactuals.change: Hold solution coefficients/constants/seed fixed; change invertible row-mixing multiplier from 1 to -1.
counterfactuals.expected: Printed initial equations and first elimination change, but the full solution vector and grading of that value remain the same.
counterfactuals.observed: Base and row-mixed records have identical keyed vectors, different prompts and operation explanations. Native grader accepts the preserved value in both. Screenshots 017/019 visually verified.
counterfactuals.justification: Equivalent row operations preserve the solution set, the central invariant of source Gauss-Jordan elimination.

shortcut_probes.subgroup: all 60 ordinary easy outputs, treating one abstention as failure
shortcut_probes.strategy: Match printed component strings only: choose the vector combining the unique modal first component and unique modal second component; abstain if modes tie. No system, solution or generation metadata is used to choose.
shortcut_probes.conclusion: 59 correct, one abstention. Baseline is uniformly choosing one of five choices (20%). This cue bypasses elimination and even substitution. Its success survives answer reordering.

delivery.result: No observed rejection or deduplication changes the sampled easy distribution. Exact delivered batch is entirely shortcut-solvable. Any selection of one of its fresh candidates retains the defect; excluding seen candidates only removes members. Read-only selection-rank reproduction is conditional on positive easy weight, not a claim about an actual learner history.

limitations: Captured inventory basis 5373; future inventory and actual learner histories/policy weights are unavailable. The stage rules were inspected; no live learner or database operations were performed.

No finite sample proves absence of every shortcut. Eleven optional source profiles were source-replayed, but broader shortcut behavior for every affine transformation of every profile is not certified.
Moderate/hard inventory replays establish this specific shortcut; this easy-job audit does not certify the full authored moderate/hard domains.
One original question lacks a key and solution. Its independently derived key is documented; no missing instructional evidence was invented.
